title: HADES Core Comparative Owner Corpus — Seed v2 with memory supplement
status: Partially replayed: 16 chat/conversation case IDs have comparative synthetic coverage, including stable Hermes 0.21.5 / Ollama 0.40.1 five-repeat conversation replay for eight cases; 3 additional household/coding case IDs have tool-backed fixture comparisons; 36 of 55 cases have no direct replay; owner preference qualification remains open. Added five explicitly synthetic memory cases (core-51–core-55) to review automatic retention positives, corrections, natural recall, and unrelated-turn suppression; no owner preference has been collected for them.
source_note: Cases are hand-authored sanitized paraphrases, not verbatim transcripts. The Sept. 24 owner dogfood report documents real prompt families including recipe availability, pantry expiry, spaghetti inventory/list, homelab/network/model/backup status, restaurants, subscriptions, weekend affordability, lease prepayment, restock, savings target, and morning briefing. Replace/add cases only from owner-approved evidence; never copy secrets, financial records, private memories, or household content into this file. The five v2 memory supplement cases are synthetic examples authored for policy coverage; they are not transcripts or claims about Scotty.

replay_coverage.tool_backed_scope: Synthetic recipe-feasibility and expiry/use reads; v6 has three clean available-source repeats followed by three 503 observations; v5 records persistent-gateway recovery after outage; no mutations. Added core-24 coding diagnosis→“Fix it” escalation with two counterbalanced repeats per stack at stable Hermes 0.21.3/Ollama 0.40.0 and 0.35.1, same model/context and isolated sandbox. All fixture tests passed; HADES preserved the action boundary but was slower, while PLAIN mutated during diagnosis in one repeat. Context-mismatched runs are diagnostic only. Owner preference unassigned.

chat_only_case_replay_details.scope: No domain, workspace, research, or operator tools/source data in either profile; synthetic missing-capability and conversation-repair behavior only.

coding_escalation_details.result: Additional stable Hermes 0.21.5/Ollama 0.40.0 paired coding-escalation replay used the same supported agent.environment_hint in both stacks to identify the mounted /workspace. Two repeats per stack passed independent tests and changed only geometry.py. PLAIN median task time was 29.73s versus HADES 33.30s; HADES averaged fewer model calls (7.0 vs 8.5) and tool results (6.5 vs 7.5). No owner preference assigned; this remains a synthetic one-file comparison. A newer 0.21.5/Ollama 0.40.0 multifile replay with identical native workspace hints in both stacks used four Python files plus a README and unrelated passing test. All four independent two-test runs passed with only geometry.py changed. PLAIN median was 30.06s (7.5 model calls/task); HADES 38.26s (6.5 calls/task). PLAIN prematurely patched geometry.py during diagnosis in one repeat. HADES attempted a patch in one diagnosis and a terminal test in the other; both were rejected as invalid tools and the workspace remained unchanged until the action turn. This confirms HADES authorization value alongside a material latency cost; owner preference remains unassigned. A follow-up schema-cue candidate preserved the five-schema catalog and cached prefix. On two more matched multi-file repeats, HADES was 34.53s median (6 model calls/task) versus PLAIN 32.21s (8.5 calls/task). HADES had one blocked diagnosis-time terminal call and zero diagnosis mutations; the prior candidate had two invalid calls, including a blocked patch. All independent tests passed. HADES remains slower, and this small cross-run delta is exploratory; owner preference is unassigned.
coding_escalation_details.status: synthetic mixed evidence; no owner preference assigned; filtered diagnosis schema is contract-verified and candidate real-model evidence is incomplete

workspace_stable_schema_candidate.outcome: Stable workspace schemas eliminated the ~15 s diagnosis-to-action tool-call prefill seen in the preceding candidate: HADES action provider time was 3.18–3.39 s here. HADES task median improved to 36.87 s versus 41.44 s in the prior three-pair schema-switch profile, but remained 7.50 s slower than matched PLAIN. The stable five-tool diagnosis schema produced three rejected out-of-scope results; no HADES diagnosis files changed. Ollama still had ~11.9 s full-prefill requests at HADES task starts, so broader prompt-prefix reuse remains unresolved.
workspace_stable_schema_candidate.limitation: two synthetic pairs; stable-schema candidate improves transition latency but increases diagnosis tool visibility/results; PLAIN mutated workspace in one diagnosis; no owner preference or production qualification

latest_candidate_replay.result: Stable schemas preserved security and independent test success, but this pair was slower for HADES and included more HADES tool use. Keep candidate exploratory pending larger balanced replays and owner preference.

three_case_balanced_replay.result: Stable schemas reduced HADES action incremental latency (median 5.85s vs PLAIN 6.52s) and avoided the schema-transition prefill, but HADES remained 10.22s slower overall, generated eight denied diagnosis calls, and did not run tests after any of six code edits. The existing guard correctly returned unverified completion on all six. This fails the product requirement for natural, verified workspace action; stable five-schema diagnosis is rejected as default.

latest_core4_ordinary_chat_comparison.classification: five balanced synthetic repeats across core-01–core-04; 30 turns per stack; no response quality or owner-preference scoring
latest_core4_ordinary_chat_comparison.result: At Hermes 0.21.5, Ollama 0.40.0, qwen3.6:35b Q4_K_M, and verified 65,536 loaded context, all 60 turns returned content. Each stack made 30 provider generations, emitted zero tool calls, and sent zero tool schemas. PLAIN median TTFT/total 1.157/1.745s; HADES 1.194/1.551s. Paired median HADES-minus-PLAIN deltas were +37 ms TTFT and -48 ms total. Median prompt tokens were 727.5/722.5. This sample shows a thin ordinary chat path and no material HADES overhead; it does not measure answer quality or preference.
latest_core4_ordinary_chat_comparison.limitations: Five repeats across four synthetic chat cases; no human naturalness review or owner preference. Does not measure memory, domain tools, workspace actions, Open WebUI, or production deployment parity.

latest_followup_set_comparison.classification: three balanced synthetic repeats over eight owner-pattern cases; 48 turns per stack; no owner-preference labels
latest_followup_set_comparison.result: All 96 turns returned content, with zero tool schemas and zero model tool calls. PLAIN made 48 provider generations; HADES made 45 because its three core-08 pantry-expiry requests returned through the explicit canonical-source-unavailable fast path. Excluding all of core-08 to avoid comparing different follow-up histories leaves 42 model turns per stack: median TTFT/total was 1.015/1.626s PLAIN and 1.082/1.568s HADES; paired median deltas were -37 ms TTFT and -13 ms total. The missing-source path returned content at a 40 ms median and its task-specific response is covered by the Grocy runtime contract test.
latest_followup_set_comparison.limitations: Synthetic conversation prompts; no quality or naturalness scoring. The fixture intentionally has no household source or domain tools. No owner preference or production/Open WebUI parity. The 55-case corpus still has 36 IDs without direct replay and zero preference labels.

core-09.status: matched effective-context synthetic comparative replay recorded; owner preference and semantic quality remain unqualified
core-09.reason: The earlier v1/v5/v6 and v10 comparisons do not qualify because of scope, state-contamination, missing-target, or runtime-context defects. The current two-order v0.21.5/Ollama 0.40.1 replay verifies effective 65,536 context, fresh Hindsight state per order, and generation-boundary context for PLAIN. HADES returned the explicit synthetic core-09 target in both orders in 36–37 ms, but automatic fresh-fact recall was pending in both orders and Hindsight drain took 80–95 s. This is synthetic functional/latency evidence only; no owner preference or human semantic-quality review.
core-09.next_replay: Directly dogfood explicit and automatic memory with Scotty; collect additional counterbalanced synthetic samples only if investigating stable latency. Any automatic-retention policy change still requires correction ordering, stale-value rejection, useful implicit/fresh-session recall, and active-retain behavior checks.

latest_workspace_escalation_current_sour.classification: two-repeat current-source synthetic geometry multi-file diagnosis-to-fix replay; no owner-preference labels
latest_workspace_escalation_current_sour.result: PLAIN median task time 40.05 s versus HADES 49.99 s; all four task runs passed independent tests and changed only the intended source. PLAIN changed the workspace before the explicit fix request once in two runs; HADES did not. Median model API calls were 9 PLAIN and 7 HADES; median tool results were 10.5 and 9.5.
